Job Title: Assistant General Counsel, Client Solutions & Wealth Management
Job Description: Guided by our company Purpose of “Inspiring well-being for our colleagues, consumers, and communities,” we are committed to building a best-in-class Law Department. We drive a high-performance culture across our Legal, Compliance, and Government Affairs functions, aligned to “what” we deliver (i.e., our goals and objectives) and “how” we demonstrate our values and behaviors while focusing on the customer. We do this through leveraging a series of core capabilities, which includes accountability, interpersonal effectiveness, ability to demonstrate business savvy, being a subject matter expert, all while supporting the Law Department’s Mission to be a trusted advocate and advisor to drive strategic solutions that advance Guardian’s purpose, priorities, and values. Do you want to be part of a collaborative Legal Team? This role will support the day-to-day operations of Guardian’s Client Solutions & Wealth Management (“CSWM”) Practice in the Law Department. You will play a critical role in providing legal advice to business partners regarding Guardian’s individual markets business with a particular emphasis on the distribution of individual insurance products, and support for the company’s broker/dealer and registered investment adviser as well as supporting its advanced markets team. A successful candidate will have excellent research and organizational skills, and business judgment as you will be required to understand and manage the laws and regulations affecting individual insurance products and wealth management offerings and provide practical advice in a rapidly changing and high-profile regulatory environment. You will also need to draft applicable agreements with distribution partners and help to facilitate the succession of general agencies. The ability to influence and drive proactive partnership in a changing business environment is critical. You will develop cross-business connections, provide industry perspective and best practices guidance while considering long-term outcomes and the needs of partners/clients when providing advice. You are Energized and excited by challenging goals; and reflected in a true sense of competitiveness and drive for results. Adaptable. You embrace ambiguity, complexity, uncertainty, and volatility. A strategic problem solver able to simplify strategic success and innovation. An effective communicator, with a proven record of influencing cross-functional teams establishing and leading strong relationships with critical partners and executive stakeholders. Able to effectively convey ideas and engage in meaningful conversations. You will Provide advice and counsel to CSWM strategies and innovation initiatives in their organizations. Participate in external forums, build partnerships internally across Guardian, and help ensure that Guardian’s CSWM business practices and policies are compliant with applicable law. Advise and assist with the implementation of new distribution and wealth management related laws and regulations. Represent the practice group as a key advisor to stakeholders to establish, inform, and maintain company-wide compliant policies. Provide effective, prompt compliance advice and support business compliance, rectifying problems, and responding to emerging challenges. Keep informed regarding pending industry changes, trends, and best practices and assess the potential impact of these changes on organizational processes. You have 7 – 10 years of experience, preferably in connection with the life insurance and/or wealth management industries. JD and licensed to practice law in New York Ability to address complex and challenging issues and communicate effectively with business leaders at all levels to optimize risk management, productivity, and communication. Ability to work in a dynamic, hands-on, fast-paced environment and respond to questions from business areas and a complex subsidiary organization. Respect for diversity and ideas of others, willingness to collaborate in a fast-paced team environment and motivation skills required. Demonstrated leadership ability in an organizational setting, corporation integrity and strong interpersonal skills are essential to success. Reporting Relationships As our Assistant General Counsel, you will report to the Associate General Counsel, CSWM. Critical Competencies / Behaviors • In accordance with our success factors of Acting with accountability, leading with the consumer at the center, committing to collaborate, communicating transparently, and connecting with empathy and compassion: • Instills Trust: Gains the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity. • Ensures Accountability: Holds self and others accountable to meet commitments • Decision Quality: Makes sound and timely decisions that propel the organization forward • Courage: Steps up to address difficult issues, communicating clearly and professionally • Customer Focus: Builds strong customer relationships and delivers customer-centric solutions • Communicates Effectively: Develops and delivers communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences. Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Data is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect, Data will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and align to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect, Data focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails, and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. This Principal Solution Architect, Data role will have a strong focus on data solution architecture, modern data platforms, data products, and AI-enabled capabilities across the Insurance business. The role bridges business, engineering, architecture, and data teams to rapidly design, build, and deploy scalable solutions that improve underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, Producer, reporting, analytics, and digital experiences. The architect will champion a data product mindset, treating data as a strategic enterprise asset with clear ownership, quality standards, reusable capabilities, governance, and measurable customer value. Key Responsibilities: Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains. Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery. Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams. Own reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency. Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards. Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units. Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy. Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints. Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns. Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs. Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture. Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability. Escalate enterprise exceptions, non-standard patterns, and enterprise-risk decisions. Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority. Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization. Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions. Influence Value Stream leaders, Product Managers, Product Owners, and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Be available for production incidents with major impact to business operations. Understand and participate across portfolio initiatives, connect dependencies and opportunities across programs to optimize solutions, increase reuse, and reduce data waste. Drive the adoption of a data product operating model across the organization. Champion data product thinking by promoting customer-centric design, product ownership, continuous improvement, and measurable business value. Establish best practices for discoverability, usability, interoperability, governance, and consumption of enterprise data products. Translate business strategy into scalable technology, data, and analytics solutions. Lead discovery workshops and data solution design sessions across underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, reporting, and digital channels. Influence enterprise technology strategy by identifying reusable capabilities and modernization opportunities. Develop reusable frameworks, accelerators, and reference architectures to improve data delivery speed, consistency, and reuse. Design modern data platforms and pipelines that support real-time and batch processing, scalable data integration, and enterprise analytics needs. Ensure high-quality, trusted data through governance, observability, lineage, metadata, and automated data quality controls. Collaborate with data engineering, product, and AI teams to operationalize AI-enabled data solutions within the data ecosystem. Foster collaboration across architecture, engineering, product management, security, data, AI, and business teams. You Have (Required Skills): Deep experience designing and governing enterprise-scale solution architectures across multiple teams and domains. Proven ability to define and drive adoption of architecture standards, frameworks, and reusable patterns. Strong understanding of modern technology ecosystems, including application architectures, APIs and delivery, integration patterns, AI, cloud platforms, and data flows. Experience balancing business priorities, technical trade-offs, and risk at an enterprise level. Demonstrated ability to operate at both strategic and hands-on levels when needed. Strong experience influencing technical direction across distributed teams without direct reporting authority. Ability to bridge business and technology, translating strategy into clear architectural direction. Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience working in regulated or risk-sensitive environments with strong awareness of governance and compliance needs. Track record of mentoring architects and engineers and elevating organizational capabilities. Experience collaborating within Agile / product-based delivery models. Experience producing product-level and team-level technical design documentation. Additional Required Data-Focused Qualifications: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field. 15+ years of experience in data integration, data architecture, data modeling, data engineering, solution architecture, or enterprise technology. Proven experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale data platforms, data products, or analytics capabilities. Strong understanding of modern data architecture principles, including data mesh, data products, metadata, governance, and domain-driven design. Experience with modern data platforms such as Databricks, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, Kafka, or similar technologies. Experience rolling out AI capabilities or AI-enabled solutions within a data ecosystem. Experience within insurance industry, including enrollment, eligibility, policy administration, billing, claims, customer data, and employer administration. Expertise in cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, APIs, microservices, and distributed systems. Strong programming and data engineering skills in Python, PySpark, and SQL. Exceptional communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management skills. Experience leading data product initiatives, including proof-of-concept development and feasibility assessment. Familiarity with product management methodologies and Agile frameworks. Success Measures: Increased adoption and reuse of enterprise data products. Improved business outcomes through product-driven data capabilities. Faster delivery of business initiatives through reusable platforms and engineering accelerators. Increased adoption of AI-powered solutions across organization. Higher data quality, trust, discoverability, and governance. Strong cross-functional alignment between business, product, engineering, architecture, and data organizations. Establishment of a sustainable product culture that treats data as a strategic enterprise asset. Job Description: Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Data is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect, Data will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and align to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect, Data focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails, and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. This Principal Solution Architect, Data role will have a strong focus on data solution architecture, modern data platforms, data products, and AI-enabled capabilities across the Insurance business. The role bridges business, engineering, architecture, and data teams to rapidly design, build, and deploy scalable solutions that improve underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, Producer, reporting, analytics, and digital experiences. The architect will champion a data product mindset, treating data as a strategic enterprise asset with clear ownership, quality standards, reusable capabilities, governance, and measurable customer value. Key Responsibilities: Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains. Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery. Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams. Own reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency. Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards. Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units. Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy. Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints. Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns. Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs. Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture. Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability. Escalate enterprise exceptions, non-standard patterns, and enterprise-risk decisions. Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority. Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization. Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions. Influence Value Stream leaders, Product Managers, Product Owners, and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Be available for production incidents with major impact to business operations. Understand and participate across portfolio initiatives, connect dependencies and opportunities across programs to optimize solutions, increase reuse, and reduce data waste. Drive the adoption of a data product operating model across the organization. Champion data product thinking by promoting customer-centric design, product ownership, continuous improvement, and measurable business value. Establish best practices for discoverability, usability, interoperability, governance, and consumption of enterprise data products. Translate business strategy into scalable technology, data, and analytics solutions. Lead discovery workshops and data solution design sessions across underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, reporting, and digital channels. Influence enterprise technology strategy by identifying reusable capabilities and modernization opportunities. Develop reusable frameworks, accelerators, and reference architectures to improve data delivery speed, consistency, and reuse. Design modern data platforms and pipelines that support real-time and batch processing, scalable data integration, and enterprise analytics needs. Ensure high-quality, trusted data through governance, observability, lineage, metadata, and automated data quality controls. Collaborate with data engineering, product, and AI teams to operationalize AI-enabled data solutions within the data ecosystem. Foster collaboration across architecture, engineering, product management, security, data, AI, and business teams. You Have (Required Qualifications) : Deep experience designing and governing enterprise-scale solution architectures across multiple teams and domains. 15+ years of experience in data integration, data architecture, data modeling, data engineering, solution architecture, or enterprise technology. Proven ability to define and drive adoption of architecture standards, frameworks, and reusable patterns. Strong understanding of modern technology ecosystems, including application architectures, APIs and delivery, integration patterns, AI, cloud platforms, and data flows. Experience balancing business priorities, technical trade-offs, and risk at an enterprise level. Demonstrated ability to operate at both strategic and hands-on levels when needed. Strong experience influencing technical direction across distributed teams without direct reporting authority. Ability to bridge business and technology, translating strategy into clear architectural direction. Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience working in regulated or risk-sensitive environments with strong awareness of governance and compliance needs. Track record of mentoring architects and engineers and elevating organizational capabilities. Experience collaborating within Agile / product-based delivery models. Experience producing product-level and team-level technical design documentation. Additional Data-Focused Qualifications Required : Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field. 15+ years of experience in data integration, data architecture, data modeling, data engineering, solution architecture, or enterprise technology. Proven experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale data platforms, data products, or analytics capabilities. Strong understanding of modern data architecture principles, including data mesh, data products, metadata, governance, and domain-driven design. Experience with modern data platforms such as Databricks, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, Kafka, or similar technologies. Experience rolling out AI capabilities or AI-enabled solutions within a data ecosystem. Experience within insurance industry, including enrollment, eligibility, policy administration, billing, claims, customer data, and employer administration. Expertise in cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, APIs, microservices, and distributed systems. Strong programming and data engineering skills in Python, PySpark, and SQL. Exceptional communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management skills. Experience leading data product initiatives, including proof-of-concept development and feasibility assessment. Familiarity with product management methodologies and Agile frameworks. Success Measures: Increased adoption and reuse of enterprise data products. Improved business outcomes through product-driven data capabilities. Faster delivery of business initiatives through reusable platforms and engineering accelerators. Increased adoption of AI-powered solutions across organization. Higher data quality, trust, discoverability, and governance. Strong cross-functional alignment between business, product, engineering, architecture, and data organizations. Job Title: Head of Portfolio Architecture, Corporate Functions
Job Description: Head of Portfolio Architecture, Corporate Functions Position Overview: The Head of Corporate Functions Architecture is a senior architecture leader responsible for shaping the end-to-end architecture and portfolio roadmap for Corporate Functions, while influencing key investment decisions required to deliver it.  The Head of Corporate Functions Architecture works closely with the Head of the Digital & Technology Corporate Functions to define, align and drive the architecture needed. This role requires expertise in end-to-end architecture that includes business processes, data, integration, AI and digital experiences to deliver scalable, secure, and compliant solutions. The role will matrix into the Head of Enterprise Architecture and drive end-to-end architecture for the Business Unit portfolio, ensuring alignment with enterprise standards while actively influencing architecture direction and investment priorities with the Enterprise Architecture team. While accountable for Corporate Functions, this role operates with enterprise-level influence, shaping cross-business outcomes, informing enterprise standards, and advising executive leadership on technology strategy. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. Key Responsibilities: Portfolio Architecture Leadership Drive architecture across multiple value streams within the business unit, ensuring cohesive, end-to-end design across platforms, products, and capabilities. Own Corporate Functions target state, portfolio roadmap, architecture priorities, investment influence, and architect leadership Shape and advance modern platform architecture, including cloud, data, and AI capabilities, to enable scalable, secure, and future-ready solutions. Improve engineering productivity and delivery speed by defining architecture patterns, standards, and operating structures that enable teams to execute effectively at scale. Define and own the Corporate Functions target-state architecture and portfolio-level roadmap aligned to enterprise architecture standards and insurance business strategy. Work with Solution Architect on scalable patterns; Principal Enterprise Architect on enterprise alignment and cross-BU tradeoffs Serve as the primary architecture advisor to the Corporate Functions Head of Digital & Technology, influencing technology strategy, investment decisions, and transformation priorities. Ensure alignment of architecture, strategy and technology to Enterprise Architecture and strategy Shapes enterprise architecture direction indirectly by contributing to standards, influencing investment decisions, and advocating for cross-business solutions through architecture governance and leadership forums. Translate insurance business objectives into capability-driven architectures, including product, corporate systems, underwriting, policy, claims, billing, and customer engagement platforms. Ensure architectural alignment across modernization initiatives, new product launches, regulatory programs, and operational efficiency efforts. Manage a team of Solution Architects Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations Responsible for building solutions to support their team Investment & Roadmap Influence Shape and influence strategic investments across: Corporate Functions areas including HR, Legal, Finance & Risk and Investments. Core platforms include Workday, Oracle and ServiceNow. Integration, APIs, and ecosystem enablement Balance near‑term delivery commitments with long‑term architectural sustainability. Identify opportunities to reduce technical debt, improve platform reuse, and accelerate time‑to‑market for insurance products. Identify opportunities that drive reuse, simplification, and consistency across business units, not just within the portfolio End‑ to ‑ End Business Unit Insurance Architecture Ownership Drive holistic architecture across: Business processes and value streams Core and surrounding application ecosystems Integration and event-driven architectures AI/ML use cases for underwriting, claims automation, fraud, and personalization Digital experiences for customers, agents, brokers, and internal users Ensure all solutions meet regulatory, risk, security, privacy, and resiliency requirements (e.g., NAIC, SOX, SOC, data privacy). Promote cloud‑native, API‑first, data‑centric, and AI‑enabled patterns where appropriate. Governance, Risk & Compliance Enforce enterprise and insurance‑specific architecture standards, principles, and guardrails. Lead or participate in architecture review and governance forums, ensuring alignment with regulatory and risk management expectations. Collaborate with security, risk, compliance, and legal partners to ensure architecture supports auditability and operational resilience. Stakeholder & Leadership Engagement Act as a strategic advisor to Corporate Functions and senior enterprise technology leadership, influencing decisions that extend beyond the Business Unit portfolio. Represent architecture needs and trade-offs in enterprise forums, shaping outcomes across business units Clearly communicate architectural direction, trade‑offs, and risk implications to both technical and non‑technical audiences. Mentor and develop architects across the portfolio, raising overall insurance architecture maturity. Team Leadership & Collaboration: Lead a team of technology architects Partner with business and technology leaders to ensure key business initiatives Partner with key enterprise technical domain architects and governance leader to apply the enterprise patterns, platforms and standards within the business unit. Co-create with Enterprise Architecture Team on business unit technology planning You have: (Required Qualifications) 7+ years of experience in technology and architecture roles, with significant experience in the insurance industry. Proven experience as a Portfolio, Domain, Product or Enterprise Architect in a large, regulated insurance or financial services environment. Deep understanding of insurance operations and systems, including policy administration, underwriting, claims, billing, and distribution. Deep understanding of Corporate system (HR, Legal, Finance and Investments) Strong expertise in end‑to‑end enterprise architecture, including business, application, data, integration, AI, and digital domains. Experience influencing senior leaders and stakeholders on technology strategy and investment decisions. Strong understanding of cloud platforms, modern integration patterns, data platforms, and AI capabilities applied to insurance use cases. Solid knowledge of insurance regulatory, risk, and compliance requirements. Core Competencies Insurance domain and systems expertise Strategic and systems thinking Portfolio planning and investment influence Executive communication and stakeholder management Architectural governance and design authority Business technology alignment in regulated environments Leadership Expectations Operates with an enterprise and insurance ‑ first mindset, balancing BU needs with enterprise outcomes. Champions modernization while respecting regulatory, operational, and risk constraints. Drives architectural consistency without slowing delivery. Develops strong architectural talent and elevates architecture practices. Location: Three days a week at a Guardian location on New York, NY, Holmdel, NJ or Bethlehem, PA. Job Title: Principal Solution Architect, Enterprise API Platform
Job Description: Principal Solution Architect, Enterprise API Platform Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Enterprise API Platform, is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders.   Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases—without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. For the Enterprise API Platform, this role serves as the strategic and technical architecture partner to the Head of Enterprise API Platform, helping translate API modernization and transformation objectives into practical, value-generating modernization decisions, reusable architecture patterns, MCP-enabled platform direction, and executable engineering outcomes. You Will (Key Responsibilities): Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams Owns reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability Escalate enterprise exceptions / non-standard patterns / enterprise-risk decisions Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions Influences Value Stream leaders, Product managers, Product Owners and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations Balance strategic and tactical decisions across API modernization, API/MCP management, API lifecycle management, domain-aligned data models, reimplementation priorities, and AI-ready API capabilities. Continuously evaluate now versus later, strategic versus tactical, reusable versus disposable, and modernization versus value delivery, ensuring meaningful outcomes through thin slices rather than broad, low-value transformation efforts. Lead enterprise API architecture patterns, technical direction, and modernization alignment across API platform engineering, internal API delivery, external API delivery, and high-impact integration initiatives. Drive API rationalization, reuse, and domain alignment by helping teams redesign APIs around business capability-based, domain-aligned data models and solve common problems once rather than repeatedly. Guide reimplementation decisions for APIs coupled to non-performant or non-scalable data sources, balancing resiliency, scalability, maintainability, delivery urgency, and longer-term architectural direction. Help shape Guardian’s API, MCP gateway, and context-layer strategy so APIs become trusted, discoverable, observable, and governed inputs into agentic AI, reusable business capabilities, and future AI-native experiences. Serve as a critical daily and weekly architecture input to the Head of Enterprise API Platform, improving decision quality, decision velocity, modernization sequencing, and executive confidence in API transformation progress. Translate complex API architecture decisions into business outcomes, helping senior technology and business leaders understand “what this means” in terms of value, risk, scalability, execution, AI enablement, and strategic platform direction. Required Qualifications: You Have: Deep experience designing and governing enterprise-scale solution architectures across multiple teams and domains Experience modernizing API ecosystems, including API management platforms, API lifecycle platforms, gateway patterns, integration patterns, performance and scalability improvements, and domain-aligned API design. Proven ability to define and drive adoption of architecture standards, frameworks, and reusable patterns Strong understanding of modern technology ecosystems (application architectures, APIs and delivery, integration patterns, AI, cloud platforms, and data flows) Experience balancing business priorities, technical trade-offs, and risk at an enterprise level Demonstrated ability to operate at both strategic and hands-on levels when needed Strong experience influencing technical direction across distributed teams without direct reporting authority Ability to bridge business and technology, translating strategy into clear architectural direction Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences Experience working in regulated or risk-sensitive environments with strong awareness of governance and compliance needs Track record of mentoring architects and engineers and elevating organizational capabilities Experience collaborating within Agile / product-based delivery models. Experience producing product-level and team-level technical design documentation. Strong engineering background with the ability to operate as a credible technical partner to engineering leaders while also shaping enterprise-level API architecture strategy. Demonstrated ability to balance pragmatic delivery with disruptive architectural thinking, including sequencing modernization work around prioritized strategic initiatives, high-visibility outcomes, and critical high-transaction-volume integrations. Strong understanding of MCP, agentic AI enablement, context-layer architecture, API observability, discoverability, governance, security, and the role of APIs as foundational inputs into AI-native enterprise capabilities. Job Title: Internal Communications Manager, Channels and Operations
Job Description: I Internal Communications Manager This role is a unique opportunity for an early-career, yet experienced communications professional to join a high-impact team shaping the future of employee communications at Guardian. Working at the intersection of communications, emerging technology, analytics, and operational excellence, this individual will help manage enterprise channels while contributing to strategic initiatives that improve how communications are delivered, measured, and experienced. Ideal candidates are intellectually curious, highly organized, and energized by solving problems, improving processes, and turning impactful ideas into reality. The role requires strong writing skills, sound editorial judgment, a service-oriented mindset, and a strong interest in data as insight for continuous improvement. If you're motivated by the opportunity to leave things better than you found them, drive meaningful change, and help a high-performing team reach its next level of impact, you'll thrive in this role. Key responsibilities Communications and channel operations Maintain high editorial and quality standards across employee-facing channels, promoting communications that are clear, concise, accurate, relevant, and aligned to each channel’s purpose. Create, curate, and manage high-quality content and templates for internal platforms, including our intranet, internal newsletter, email campaigns, digital signage, and enterprise social platform. Utilize content management systems (CMS) for the day-to-day management and publishing across internal communication channels, ensuring that content is both easily accessible to employees and easily maintained by communications team members. Support recurring content review and auditing workflows to help ensure employee-facing information remains current, accurate, useful, and well managed. Coordinate with Internal Communications, Marketing, IT, and vendor teams to maintain channel operations and communications enablement tools as needed. Uphold governance and brand guidelines across internal communication channels to positively reflect company identity and culture while enabling positive employee experiences. Monitor and assess the performance of internal communication efforts, using insights to help refine approaches and identify best practices. Provide executional and administrative support for internal communications and channel operations, including documentation and refinement of protocols, templates, standard communications materials, and other resources for enablement. Stakeholder support and counsel Advise business partners, communicators, and channel users on optimal use of enterprise communications channels for their audiences and goals. Serve as a collaborative thought partner on channel and communications operations initiatives, bringing sound judgment, practical recommendations, and a service mindset. Assist as needed with cross-training and support to employees on the use of internal communication tools and platforms. Leverage subject matter expertise to serve as a trusted knowledge manager for our internal network of communicators, facilitating knowledge sharing, documentation, and continuous learning. Continuous improvement and innovation Contribute data, insights, and proven best practices to efforts to enhance the effectiveness and engagement for internal communications. Support technology adoption and AI transformation by learning new tools and methodologies, translating best practices into practical resources and recommending ways to improve how the team works. Further champion AI transformation by ideating, exploring, testing, and implementing AI agents and tools to enable communications. Foster a culture of continuous improvement by soliciting and incorporating feedback from colleagues and stakeholders to improve processes, reduce bottlenecks, and enhance effectiveness. Stay abreast of industry trends and best practices in internal communications, channel operations, and web content management. Qualifications and skills Required Bachelor's degree in Communications, Marketing, or Journalism. 3-6 years of experience in internal communications or employee engagement. Exceptional writing, editing, and proofreading skills, with an eye for detail and accuracy. Strongly preferred Experience managing internal channels, such as intranets, digital signage, and email newsletters and/or campaigns. Special consideration will be given to candidates who: Are proficient with key tools ― SharePoint, Viva Engage, Power platform, and/or internal communications measurement platforms such as SWOOP Analytics and tyGraph. Have consulting experience in a management consulting firm environment. Working conditions Hybrid work arrangement, requiring 3 days in the office each week. This role can be based in our New York, NY, or Boston, MA, office. Options for assignment to another tristate hub office — Holmdel, NJ, or Stamford, CT —may be considered for highly qualified candidate Salary Range: $82,770.00 - $135,975.00 The salary range reflected above is a good faith estimate of base pay for the primary location of the position. Through a combination of analytics, training, and process oversight, this position helps drive operational excellence, enhance team capability, and improve the overall customer and advisor experience. Job Title: Head of AI Platform Engineering - Execution Plane
Job Description: As the Head of AI Platform Engineering – Execution Plane, you will lead the development and implementation of our enterprise platform’s execution layer including management of agentic AI workloads, model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, MCP servers, orchestration frameworks, or AI execution engines. You will: You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, stakeholders, and technology partners to develop and integrate automation solutions that drive business growth, improve customer experiences, and reduce operational costs. You have: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, engineering, management or a related field. Strong people leadership experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and developing senior technical talent. Deep hands-on technical background designing, building, and operating production-grade distributed systems, AI/ML platforms, data platforms, or cloud-native runtime services. Experience leading teams responsible for the execution layer of a platform, including runtime services, model inference, retrieval, orchestration, tool invocation, workflow execution, or production AI operations. Ability to own the roadmap and delivery for execution plane capabilities such as model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, runtime adapters, MCP services, knowledge bases, retrieval pipelines, inference services, and deployment patterns. Strong understanding of data access patterns, enterprise APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, vector/search systems, context engineering, and governed access to systems of record. Experience building reliable, scalable, low-latency execution services with clear contracts, strong observability, graceful degradation, retry patterns, rate limits, and operational resilience. Ability to partner with control plane, developer experience, data engineering, security, architecture, operations, and domain application teams to ensure execution technologies operate behind governed platform interfaces. Proven ability to drive engineering excellence through design reviews, architecture standards, testing, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, incident response, SLOs, runbooks, and production support mechanisms. Strong understanding of enterprise security and compliance requirements for runtime execution, including identity propagation, auditability, data handling, least privilege access, secrets management, and environment isolation. Strong communication and influence skills, with the ability to simplify complex runtime, data, and AI execution topics for senior stakeholders while aligning teams around reusable platform patterns. You will: Experience with agentic AI systems, LLM platforms, model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, MCP servers, orchestration frameworks, or AI execution engines. Experience with AWS-based AI execution services and cloud-native patterns, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker, Lambda, Step Functions, API Gateway, EKS, DynamoDB, S3, IAM, CloudWatch, and related DevOps tooling. Familiarity with RAG systems, enterprise search, vector databases, embedding models, rerankers, knowledge bases, context engineering, and governed retrieval from enterprise data sources. Experience designing multi-tenant runtime platforms with environment isolation, workload identities, RBAC/ABAC, cross-account access patterns, quotas, throttling, and secure service-to-service communication. Background in MLOps, LLMOps, AIOps, model lifecycle management, evaluation pipelines, model serving, inference optimization, or production AI operations. Experience with observability for AI workloads, including distributed tracing, token usage, latency, model/tool errors, cost attribution, quality metrics, safety metrics, and operational dashboards. Experience with performance, scalability, and cost optimization for high-volume runtime services, including caching, batching, streaming, load testing, capacity planning, and GPU/CPU optimization where applicable. Experience building reusable platform abstractions, SDKs, runtime adapters, reference architectures, or deployment templates that make execution technologies portable across vendors and use cases. Experience integrating enterprise tools, APIs, data services, and workflow systems through governed connectors rather than point-to-point application wiring. Comfort operating in a regulated, matrixed environment where production safety, auditability, resiliency, and vendor optionality are core design principles. Job Description: The Principal Enterprise Architect is a senior architecture leader responsible for shaping, guiding, and advancing enterprise architecture across the organization. Reporting to the Head of Enterprise Architecture and Engineering Enablement , this role translates enterprise strategy into practical architecture direction, standards, target-state designs, and transition roadmaps across business capabilities, applications, platforms, data, integration, cloud, security, and emerging technology domains. While architecture is foundation al, the Principal Enterprise Architect will be responsible for design ing enterprise solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders . Where applicable the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale for the enterprise. This position plays a critical role in connecting enterprise strategy to federated execution. The Principal Enterprise Architect partners with architecture, engineering, platform, security, data, and business technology leaders to ensure material technology decisions align with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, modernization priorities, and governance requirements. The role requires strong strategic thinking, architecture breadth, executive communication, and the ability to influence across a large, complex, and federated enterprise environment. The Principal Enterprise Architect provides architecture leadership and recommendations on material technology decisions and has delegated authority within the enterprise architecture operating model as assigned by the Head of Enterprise Architecture. The role is expected to escalate decisions with enterprise-wide impact, non-standard exceptions, or significant risk implications. Key Responsibilities: Enterprise Architecture Leadership Support the Head of Enterprise Architecture in developing and evolving enterprise architecture strategy , principles, standards, and target-state roadmaps. Define and maintain architecture perspectives across business, application, data, integration, cloud, platform, security, and AI-related capabilities as applicable. Own enterprise standards, target state, governance, exceptions, material technology decision frameworks Translate enterprise strategy and target-state direction into practical guidance for domain architecture and engineering teams. Promote alignment across business units, shared services, and technology domains. Strategic Architecture and Transformation Provide architecture leadership for major strategic initiatives, modernization programs, and enterprise-impacting technology decisions. Assess architecture options and recommend solutions that balance business value, cost, risk, resilience, time to market, and long-term maintainability. Support enterprise transformation through simplification, rationalization, modernization, and platform reuse. Identify opportunities to reduce duplication, retire legacy complexity, and improve interoperability across the enterprise. Governance and Decision Support Participate in and support enterprise architecture governance, standards councils, review boards, and strategic decision forums. Evaluate material technology decisions using approved enterprise frameworks, including buy, build, reuse, partner, and retire options. Review architecture proposals for compliance with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, and risk requirements. Support management of architecture exceptions, including rationale, risk analysis, remediation paths, and time-bound approvals. Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations Cross-Functional Partnership Partner with federated domain architects, platform leaders, engineering teams, data and AI teams, security, infrastructure, and business technology leaders to drive alignment. Facilitate resolution of cross-domain design issues, architecture conflicts, and overlapping capability decisions. Act as a trusted advisor to leaders across technology and business-aligned delivery organizations. Ensure architecture direction is understood and applied consistently across federated teams. Works with Business Unit heads and principal solution architects to translate enterprise direction into federated execution. Risk, Security, and Resilience Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, resilience, recoverability, and regulatory considerations into architecture guidance and recommendations. Partner with risk, security, and compliance stakeholders to ensure technology decisions align with enterprise control requirements. Job Description: The Enterprise Data Solutions & Operations (EDSO) team within the Digital & Technology (D-T) function is looking to staff a Head of Data Solutions (the ‘Role’) for our FPRS/CSWM line of business. This role will work closely with core FPRS/CSWM business value streams (e.g., distribution mgmt., shop, purchasing, service, claims, etc.) to define, shape, prioritize and lead the delivery and evolution of key data and information product (‘Products’) solutions supporting business objectives. More specifically, this role will drive the capture and planning for new demand of features and/or enhancements to Guardian’s data Products as articulated by key business leaders from one or more key value stream and/or the respective FPRS/CSWM FP&A functional BI leader. These data Products include everything from consumer-facing analytics (reports/dashboards), to inter/intra-application data services (APIs/extracts/shares), to data services supporting AI/GenAI automation, to the underlying data definitions and reference data that define the FPRS/CSWM businesses. In addition, this role will have accountability for planning and delivering strategic data initiatives within one or more FPRS/CSWM value stream, collaborating with the value stream Digital & Tech (D&T) Leader, the value stream Business Leader, the value stream Product Delivery Managers (PDMs), and the value stream Product Owners(POs)) to identify/scope/size and execute key data needs, and to identify and raise new opportunities for data activation/adoption. A key aspect of the role will be to balance the needs across value stream demands, soliciting/recommending priorities, and in turn, incorporating and aligning these priorities into a roadmap and plan for delivery, including resource planning (business SMEs, UAT participants, etc.), training, and activation in support of full value realization. Finally, the FPRS/CSWM Data Solution Head will direct the data steward(s) in their charter to continuously capture metadata related to all data elements (e.g., definition, quality standards, calculation logic, SLA requirements, etc.), and to report/coordinate any data quality issues/SLA breaches/definitional changes to the same. From a strategic management perspective, the role will bring a keen understanding of value stream processes, supporting applications and key data elements. Moreover, the role will establish and nurture relationships with both value stream executive leadership, as well as functional and analytic SMEs in the value stream teams to keep a pulse on the latent needs and direction of the business. Using these relationships, the role will anticipate future data needs, constantly updating and communicating the backlog of features to be addressed in the data/info product roadmap - all in close coordination with business partners in the FPRS/CSWM FP&A analytics team(s). From an org management perspective, the Role will directly manage and grow a team of data product owners (DPOs).  These DPOs will be aligned with FPRS/CSWM value stream data products and will drive the execution of new build features/enhancements to their respective data products. In addition, the Role will manage both direct (EDSO FPRS/CSWM Solution Engineering team members, EDSO FPRS/CSWM Data Product Owners) and indirect (D&T Solution & Data Architecture resources, and D&T Data Governance resources), in order to drive the successful delivery of data products, as well as to help foster the development of the next generation of D&T data leaders, You are: You are a highly independent senior manager with the ability to (or rapidly become) conversant in life insurance and wealth management products and their respective business processes. You have an aptitude for using and shaping data solutions in support of business objectives and are able to clearly articulate the value that can be attributable to data/info products. You are highly organized, staying abreast of multiple stakeholders’ priorities, the status of multiple parallel initiatives/projects/data products, and the state of value realization and adoption for production data assets. You communicate fluidly and extemporaneously, able to articulate how data solution functionality will meet business needs in a brief, non-technical manner. While you may not be a recent ‘hands on keyboards’ technologist (you may even have come from a business or analytical background), you have a deep understanding of data and analytic technologies, architectural principles, and you aren’t afraid to dig into data models and pipeline logic. Finally, you are reliable in terms of your commitments, honest and brave with issues/escalations, and have a client service mentality. You have: 15+ years of experience with an escalating competency in data and analytic solutions BS or BA required; MS or MBA preferred 3+ years working in an agile environment 3+ years of experience managing staff/teams, potentially (preferably) with geographically diverse teams, often organized on a product delivery basis (highly matrixed) 5+ years of experience with standard program management tools (such as JIRA, AgileCraft, ATIIM, etc.), as well as desktop collaboration/ideation tools (Sharepoint, MSOffice, OneDrive, Lucid, Draw.io, etc.) Experience in life insurance and wealth management products and industry preferred (e.g., whole/term/universal/supplemental/etc., as well as , FIA, portfolio/client management tools for FAs/Brokers, etc.) Experience with enterprise data management principles such as data ownership/stewardship (experience as a data domain steward or data product owner would be a plus) Ability to document and capture business requirements in detail, including metric calculation logic, quality/timeliness expectations, analytic functionality, hierarchies, etc., as well as functional user journeys as they relate to data solutions A client focus with strong verbal and written communication skills, able to manage multiple stakeholders and creatively align their interests, and able to lead workshops on ideation/requirements with little preparation Strong organizational and time management skills; ability to multi-task and driving teams to meet aggressive delivery commitments Proactive problem-solving and information research skills Ability to manage/mentor earlier tenure and/or less experienced staff to help grow future leaders and deepen value stream knowledge on the broader team Ability to accept change in stride, remaining flexible due to changing business needs/priorities Natural ‘teacher’, able to coach business partners on optimal use of data assets to meet stated/latent business needs Comfort with/knowledge of analytic tools such as Tableau, PowerBI, Databricks, SQL, etc. Deep knowledge/experience with data lakehouse principles and data management tooling (e.g., Databricks, Fivetran, Collibra, SQL/SparkSQL/Python, etc.) Able to see the “big picture” and influence/engage others to meet common goals You Will: Engage in business value stream Counseling: Develop deep and trust-based relationships with value stream stakeholders Consult with value stream business partners to identify and shape new and existing ways for data to enable business processes and aspirations Lead decisioning/status, prioritization, and ideation meetings with various stakeholder groups, from executives to expert practitioners as it relates to new data/info products and/or data service delivery Maintain a data product and info product roadmap supported by technical capabilities to keep business abreast of vision and timing Capture demand and stay responsive to emergent needs from business value stream business partners (from the value stream leads to the application PDMs) Demonstrate expertise in processes and their supporting data assets by educating business partners (directly 1:1, in formal training sessions, and informally), and by providing direct feedback to value stream owners on usage characteristics of value stream data solutions Product Management: Serve as the primary owner of FPRS/CSWM value stream data product strategy, managing the roadmap for ongoing enhancements and new capabilities Accountable for the overall agile delivery of new data sources and products, establishing the features, business rules and test conditions with business input, and in response, coordinating the explosion of these features into technical detail via your team of DPOs In concert with EDSO platform engineering team members, contribute to the evaluation of proposed tools, technologies, and platforms from a business lens Contribute to ongoing delivery/capacity planning, ensuring value stream needs are appropriately resourced/planned for delivery with eDSO solution engineers/architects Manage testing, both directly as a point tester and via coordination with key business SMEs Partner with value Job Description: Job Summary The Level III Business Intelligence Analyst is responsible for leading business intelligence workstreams, translating business needs into data-driven solutions, and delivering accurate, reliable, and actionable reporting and analytics. This role partners closely with business and technology stakeholders to gather requirements, design BI solutions, establish standards, support data quality, and help business partners use information to identify trends, patterns, risks, and opportunities. Key Responsibilities Create visualizations that support quick consumption, collaboration, exploration, transparency, and storytelling with information. Train end users on reports, dashboards, patterns, and anomalies, and mentor internal team members on processes, policies, procedures, and BI practices. Analyze business problems, develop models, and provide insights that help explain trends, patterns, anomalies, and business performance. Recommend key performance indicators for multiple business units and explain how metrics are calculated and used. Lead BI project workstreams, including requirements gathering, scope development, technical design, development, testing, and delivery. Create and maintain templates, development standards, reporting standards, and visualization standards for team use. Partner with IT and business stakeholders to design BI solutions that support operational decision-making and business strategy. Develop and optimize complex SQL queries using views, stored procedures, table-valued functions, subqueries, indexing concepts, execution plans, and multiple databases. Apply deep knowledge of relevant databases, data structures, and business data sources to deliver accurate and trusted reporting products. Influence business partners on BI best practices, report design, data interpretation, and prioritization of work. Lead testing scenario creation and execution, audit work for accuracy, and ensure delivered products meet high data quality standards. Research new BI technologies, interface with vendors, participate in vendor evaluations, and recommend tools or approaches that improve analytics capabilities. Required Qualifications Experience developing, maintaining, and improving business intelligence reports, dashboards, metrics, and analytical solutions. Strong SQL skills, including experience with complex queries, database objects, functions, joins, indexing concepts, and performance considerations. Deep understanding of BI tools, reporting functionality, data visualization principles, and how business users consume analytics. Ability to gather and translate business requirements into clear technical and analytical deliverables. Demonstrated ability to lead internal workstreams, manage multiple priorities, and influence stakeholders on sequencing and prioritization. Experience validating data, creating test scenarios, executing test plans, and ensuring high-quality deliverables. Ability to identify patterns, trends, correlations, anomalies, and business implications from complex data. Strong communication skills with the ability to explain metrics, findings, recommendations, and data limitations to technical and non-technical audiences. Experience mentoring peers or team members on BI processes, reporting standards, data interpretation, or tool usage. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting multiple business units or cross-functional reporting initiatives. Experience with BI platforms such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar visualization and dashboarding tools. Experience with Data Blending tools such as Alteryx, DataIku, Informatica, Snaplogic, or similar. Experience researching, evaluating, or recommending new reporting, analytics, or data technology capabilities. Understanding of data security processes, dashboard access, database access, and related ticketing or access request workflows. Familiarity with advanced analytics concepts and how predictive or prescriptive analytics can support business decision-making. Core Competencies Technical proficiency in SQL, BI tools, reporting standards, data validation, and dashboard development. Business acumen with the ability to recommend KPIs, understand business unit needs, and connect analysis to strategic priorities. Analytical thinking with the ability to research business problems, create models, and deliver meaningful insights. Process improvement mindset with the ability to create standards, lead internal workstreams, and improve reporting practices. Stakeholder influence with the ability to guide business partners on best practices, prioritization, and effective use of data. Job Description: Is the opportunity to join a culture where “We Do the Right Thing,” and “We Courageously Shape Our Future Together” important to you? If so, Guardian is seeking a motivated individual to join our team as a Finance Transformation Lead. This role is responsible for driving strategic transformation initiatives across the Finance organization to improve performance, optimize processes, advance AI-enabled capabilities, and strengthen data-driven decision-making. Reporting to the Head of Finance & Risk Transformation, Strategy and Operations, s/he will partner closely with Finance, Technology, Risk, Operations, Data, and business leaders to design and implement future-state operating models, modernize planning and reporting processes, and deliver sustainable business value. AI enablement is a core accountability This leader will advance the organization's AI-enabled Finance strategy by embedding Generative AI, intelligent automation, predictive analytics, and agentic AI capabilities into Finance processes, operating models, and ways of working, while ensuring responsible adoption, governance, risk management, and measurable value realization. You will Key Responsibilities Transformation Strategy & Execution Develop and execute Finance transformation strategies aligned with business and enterprise objectives. Lead large-scale transformation initiatives spanning Finance processes, operating models, systems, data, controls, and organizational capabilities. Manage transformation roadmaps, implementation plans, milestones, dependencies, and value realization objectives. Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, effectiveness, decision support, governance, and stakeholder experience. Drive continuous improvement and innovation across Finance functions. AI Enablement & Digital Innovation Lead the Finance AI strategy and roadmap, identifying opportunities to leverage Generative AI, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, and agentic AI solutions to improve productivity, decision-making, and business outcomes. Partner with Finance leaders to identify, prioritize, and scale high-value AI use cases across FP&A, forecasting, management reporting, expense management, financial close, workforce planning, and decision support. Drive adoption of enterprise AI capabilities, including Microsoft Copilot, Claude, AI agents, and emerging technologies, ensuring alignment with business priorities and governance expectations. Establish frameworks for AI use case intake, evaluation, prioritization, value realization, adoption measurement, and ongoing performance monitoring. Collaborate with Technology, Data, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Information Security teams to ensure responsible AI adoption and adherence to enterprise governance standards. Lead AI-related change management efforts, including communications, training, stakeholder engagement, and capability-building programs to increase AI literacy across Finance. Measure and track AI adoption, productivity gains, capacity creation, cost savings, decision quality improvements, and other business outcomes. Monitor emerging AI trends, technologies, and industry best practices, translating innovation into actionable opportunities for Finance. Operating Model & Process Transformation Design and implement future-state Finance operating models, governance structures, and service delivery frameworks. Lead process optimization across FP&A, forecasting and budgeting, management reporting, financial close and consolidation, business performance management, expense management, and capital planning. Promote standardization, automation, simplification, and scalable ways of working across Finance processes. Assess organizational readiness, capability gaps, role impacts, and process changes required to sustain transformation outcomes. Technology, Data & Analytics Enablement Partner with Technology and Data teams to lead implementation of Finance platforms, reporting solutions, analytics capabilities, and digital tools. Support transformation initiatives involving ERP modernization, Oracle Planning/EPM, enterprise performance management, reporting platforms, AI-enabled workflows, and automation solutions. Translate business requirements into technology-enabled solutions, user stories, process designs, and implementation roadmaps. Strengthen Finance data quality, consistency, transparency, and accessibility to support analytics, forecasting, and AI-enabled insights. Stakeholder Management, Governance & Change Leadership Serve as a trusted advisor to Finance executives, senior stakeholders, and cross-functional partners. Facilitate executive workshops, strategic planning sessions, use case prioritization discussions, and operating model design conversations. Establish governance structures, reporting mechanisms, risk management routines, and escalation channels for transformation initiatives. Manage vendor, consulting partner, and cross-functional delivery relationships as required. Lead change management, communications, training, and stakeholder engagement activities that support adoption and sustained behavior change. You have Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, Engineering, Information Systems, Data Analytics, or a related field. 8+ years of Finance, consulting, transformation, strategy, technology enablement, or program management experience. 5+ years leading large-scale Finance transformation initiatives or enterprise change programs. Experience leading AI, Generative AI, automation, digital transformation, or advanced analytics initiatives within Finance or related business functions. Demonstrated ability to identify, prioritize, and implement AI use cases that deliver measurable business value. Strong understanding of Finance operating models, planning, forecasting, reporting, expense management, and performance management processes. Experience developing transformation roadmaps, business cases, benefits realization plans, and executive-level presentations. Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence senior stakeholders across business, technology, data, risk, and operations. Strong analytical, facilitation, problem-solving, communication, and executive storytelling skills. Preferred Qualifications MBA, CPA, CFA, PMP, Lean Six Sigma, Agile, SAFe, or other relevant advanced degree or certification. Experience within Financial Services, Insurance, Banking, Risk Management, or other highly regulated industries. Experience implementing Oracle Planning, Oracle EPM Cloud, Hyperion, SAP, Workday, Anaplan, or similar Finance platforms. Experience with Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Azure AI, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, agent-based AI solutions, workflow automation, or similar platforms. Knowledge of Responsible AI, AI governance, model risk management, data governance, privacy, information security, and adoption frameworks. Consulting experience with a leading management consulting firm or enterprise transformation practice. Key Competencies Strategic Leadership Enterprise mindset, strategic planning, business acumen, vision-setting, prioritization, and decision-making. Transformation Delivery Program leadership, portfolio management, roadmap execution, risk management, change leadership, and benefits realization. AI & Digital Enablement Generative AI adoption, AI use case identification, intelligent automation, analytics, responsible AI practices, and innovation management. Finance Expertise FP&A, forecasting, reporting, performance management, expense management, operating model design, and process optimization. Relationship Management Executive presence, stakeholder influence, facilitation, cross-functional partnership, and communication. Job Title: Lead Financial & Business Analyst - Wealth Management
Job Description: Is the opportunity to join a culture where “We Do the Right Thing,” and “We Courageously Shape Our Future Together” important to you? If so, Guardian is seeking a resolute motivated individual to join our team as a Lead Financial Business Analyst. The Lead Financial Business Analyst for Client Solutions and Wealth Management (CSWM) leads the development of analytics and financial planning initiatives that drive actionable insights and support strategic decision-making across the CSWM business. This role partners closely with business leaders to deliver robust financial models, forecasts, and performance analyses, ensuring the organization achieves its financial and operational objectives. You will: Analyze business performance, financial results, and key metrics to identify trends, risks, and opportunities. Lead the creation and maintenance of financial models to support budgeting, forecasting, and strategic initiatives for CSWM. Proactively collaborate with subject matter experts across the business to acquire knowledge necessary to build and interpret analytics. Prepare analytical illustrations to be shared with CSWM leaders and business area SMEs. Lead the creation and maintenance of financial models to support budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning for CSWM. Continuously improve analytical processes and tools to enhance efficiency and insight generation. You are: Resourceful and relentlessly curious. Comfortable transforming a conceptual analytical framework into tangible insights by seeing the value of relationships between data and the business rules and processes that derive and inform the data. Comfortable operating with minimal oversight, you independently locate, reconcile, and validate data, flagging and resolving issues before they become problems. You're a confident communicator who develops a deep understanding of complex topics and translates results for stakeholders in clear, non-technical terms, iterating with leadership and subject-matter experts to rationalize and refine the value of your analysis. You have: 5+ years’ experience developing and presenting financial and business analytics. 5+ years’ experience analyzing financial statements and interpreting results. Advanced analytical aptitude, and drive to acquire knowledge/context necessary to perfect analysis. Experience working across multiple business areas and/or lines of business (e.g., sales, finance, life, disability), and demonstrating knowledge of the concepts, processes, and datasets inherent to those environments. Advanced experience with Excel and other data/analytics tools, and comfort working with large, complex datasets.
